title: Discover clinical variables
integration_notes: Use one evidence card per call. Attach provenance and machine names in Python. The response schema matches the adopted discovery validator. The caller determines when a second review is needed.

title: Review excerpts for overlooked clinical variables
integration_notes: Use one evidence card per call. Attach provenance and machine names in Python. The response schema matches the adopted discovery validator. The caller determines when a second review is needed.

title: Group names for the same clinical variable
integration_notes: Resolve semantic labels, enforce disjoint membership/protections, preserve unmentioned variables, and normalize names in Python.

title: Define how to measure one clinical variable
integration_notes: Keep identity/protections in Python; validate the definition and conflict rules. Translate the model's unit string or category list into the legacy categories_or_unit array. Latest is the proposed prompt default for ordinary repeated measurements. Study-specific measurement restrictions must be written directly into a feature definition when needed.

title: Extract one patient's declared variables
integration_notes: Python owns patient identity, internal column names, envelopes, and validation. Supply the appropriate record text; omit record_scope and any explanation of upstream eligibility handling.

title: Update values after reading more of a patient's record
integration_notes: Python keeps patient/chunk IDs and ordering. Route mode aggregation through occurrence extraction so Python can count observations. State translation and bookkeeping are excluded from the model instructions.

title: Extract clinical observations and their supporting words
integration_notes: Python locates exact quotations, attaches source/patient/page IDs, normalizes dates, and reconciles observations. Validate ambiguous quote matches rather than assigning arbitrary offsets.

title: Match a phrase to an existing clinical category
integration_notes: Deduplicate tokens and handle IDs/occurrences in Python. Use deterministic normalization where it suffices.

title: Clarify instructions after extraction failures
integration_notes: Python attaches identity and restricts revisions to the allowed definition fields, then controls re-extraction. Ordinary category synonyms can use the category-mapping path.

title: Choose a common representation for one clinical variable
integration_notes: Python parses supported numerical constraints and creates exhaustive, nonoverlapping intervals, including complements. A typed adapter or explicit clarification path is required for unparsed semantics. Insufficient definitions must be handled explicitly; the LLM does not need to know the bin-construction mechanism.

title: Interpret a new phrase using defined categories
integration_notes: Python keeps the representation fixed, extends the token map, and handles identities. This proposed call remains limited to training map construction.

title: Review a clinical measurement definition using extraction summaries
integration_notes: Python preserves the clinical target and roles, distinguishes current/historical count populations, and controls revisions and re-extraction.

title: Combine equivalent extracted measurements
integration_notes: Python computes paired agreement, compiles deterministic coalescing/recodes, checks losslessness, and retains IDs. This proposal requires those diagnostics and adapters before use.

title: Assess a clinical variable's confounder and modifier roles
integration_notes: Python supplies genuine study context and coherent evidence availability, attaches identity/provenance, preserves investigator-locked roles, and validates assignments. Qualitative assessments require evaluation before adoption.

title: Group variables into clinical themes
integration_notes: Python checks coverage, assigns theme IDs, and attaches member evidence. Theme grouping leaves measurement columns intact.

title: Combine overlapping clinical themes
integration_notes: Python unions members/provenance and preserves unchanged themes. Context limits are handled by batching/retrieval rather than forcing unrelated semantic merges.

title: Assess roles using several models and clinical themes
integration_notes: Python attaches feature/evidence IDs, retains locked roles, and applies routing. This prompt only contains the clinical decision and evidence needed to make it.

title: Rank clinical variables by modifier evidence
integration_notes: Python resolves labels, orders genuine ties deterministically, assigns numerical ranks, and chooses a modifier count through validation. Those mechanics are absent from the model task.

title: Compare two potential effect modifiers
integration_notes: Python selects the current front candidates, preserves within-list order, caches comparisons, and produces the merged ranking. Pairwise merging still requires cost and order-sensitivity evaluation.

title: Explain a variable's recorded selection decision
integration_notes: Python attaches this explanation without changing fixed numerical decisions. A failed annotation does not alter selection.

title: Identify clinical concepts behind candidate modifiers
integration_notes: Python computes recurrence and coverage, keeps the review blinded to oracle/test outcomes, and checks membership. This remains an experimental interpretation proposal.

title: Correct an extraction response after a validation error
integration_notes: Python retains the original task/input, formats precise errors, controls reasoning and retry budgets, and validates the complete response. Split requests or increase output space when necessary; the repair prompt does not explain those mechanics.

title: Complete a truncated extraction response
integration_notes: Python retains the original task/input, formats precise errors, controls reasoning and retry budgets, and validates the complete response. Split requests or increase output space when necessary; the repair prompt does not explain those mechanics.
